name: Petrov Defense
blurb: Black meets 2.Nf3 by counterattacking e4 instead of defending e5. One of the most solid defences to 1.e4, used by many world-class players.

lines.name: Classical Attack, Marshall Variation, Chinese Gambit

ideas.e4 e5: Claims the centre with the e-pawn, matching White.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6: The Petrov. Black counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6: Kicks the knight first. Taking on e4 at once runs into Qe2, attacking the knight along the e-file.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4: Now Black wins the pawn back, and material is level.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5: Supports the e4 knight with a pawn.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3: Develops the bishop and gets ready to castle.
Supports d5 with another pawn, so White's c4 does not break up Black's centre.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 exd4: Takes the pawn. Black's knight on f6 is still attacking e4.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5 Ne4: The knight steps forward to a central square instead of going back.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7: Against the Cochrane Gambit, Black takes the knight. The king is exposed, but a whole piece is worth more than the two pawns White got.
ideas.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6: Against the Three Knights, Black mirrors White's development.
